headline: Trading firms Jump and DRW are moving into a new market for buying and selling access to AI computing power.
score_reason: Early-stage market-structure story read in one specialist outlet; interesting but small so far.
importance_line: Companies that need AI computing power and the trading firms taking the other side are affected first, though the exchange-listed futures have not yet launched and are still awaiting regulatory review.
summary: TokenPost reports that Jump Trading plans to take positions in contracts tied to computing capacity, including futures with no expiry date, while DRW has signed a deal for a dedicated cluster of Nvidia Blackwell B300 chips with the cloud provider QumulusAI. It adds that CME Group has proposed futures based on GPU rental price indexes, but their launch, first targeted for 5 Oct, has been pushed to later this year.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; TokenPost's article on the same developments read and credited (it does not cite Bloomberg). Single specialist outlet.
